detailed_review.score_reasoning: Baseline 3 = 10 - 7, term by term: F1 type-mixture 2, F2 stale-claim 1, F3 third-person reader 1, F4 status-log 1, F7 first-person heading 1, F5 British spelling 0.5, F6 stale last_reviewed 0.5. After 5 = 10 - 4.5, floored from 5.5: F1 2, F2 1, F4 1, F6 0.5 remain open. Delta +2. Three things this number is not. It is not a verdict on the T13 change, which I checked at source and found correct: wiki/updates.md:8 now reads installing.md, line 105 links [Installing Hearth](installing.md) with the destination's own frontmatter title as link text per wiki/style-guide.md:160-165, wiki/installing.md:91 carries `## Open Hearth for the first time on macOS` with the right-click steps the sentence claims at lines 96-98, and no occurrence of install-macos survives on the page. It is not a linter score: the five warnings the linter reports here, bold-lead at 21, 26, 60 and 67 and long-paragraph at 132, are excluded by rule and cost nothing, which is why no term-list-as-prose finding appears despite the bolded-lead paragraphs being the page's most visible surface defect. And it is not a distance travelled: 5 grades the page as it stands, where nearly two thirds of the open penalty is one structural fact that no sentence-level edit can reach.
detailed_review.what_worked: F3 is the change a reader will feel. The page was the only top-level article in wiki/ that never said you, and it was doing it in the one paragraph where it matters most, telling the reader that an update must never touch home/, where the memory and journal live. Whose memory? It now says yours. The same edit closes a seam with wiki/installing.md, which addresses the reader directly and links here at line 258, so a reader crossing between them no longer changes person mid-journey. F7 removes the corpus's only unattributed narrator from a published page: a grep of wiki/ for first-person constructions returns hits under wiki/raw/, where staged research is entitled to them, one quoted persona line, and this heading. A reader now gets a recommendation with a rationale instead of an anonymous opinion, and the five items under it were already impersonal, so nothing else had to move. F5 is small and real: the page spelled a term one way and the install page it links to spelled it the other.
detailed_review.what_holds_score_down: F1, worth 2 of the 4.5, is the page. The first six sections are a good concept article: what an update is, why it is 30 MB and not 3.8 GB, what already works with the provisioner quoted verbatim and correctly, what is missing, two designs, and an honest limit. Then the register changes three times. §The decision underneath: signing is a decision record with a cost, two consequences and no decision. §The order the work should land in is a build order, which is tasks/ material by CLAUDE.md. §What this closes elsewhere is bookkeeping for another page. A reader sent here from installing.md for the design gets all three. F4, worth 1, has a second victim: because the four answers live here, wiki/backend/build-pipeline.md still presents settled questions as open, which is exactly the failure wiki/style-guide.md:173-180 exists to prevent, and only a reader who happens to land on this page learns the difference. F2, worth 1, is the quietest and the one I would most want settled: the page quotes the install record's own comment, and that string is nowhere in this tree, while the provision.rs quotation three paragraphs above it is exact. One verified quotation next to one that cannot be found is worse than neither, because a reader who checks the second has no way to know the first is sound. F6, worth 0.5, is the date. Two nits are visible and unscored, named here rather than padded into found[]: line 52 says it is simply not reachable, where the intensifier is doing nothing that wiki/style-guide.md:101 wants kept, and line 130 slips into the past tense, a machine that had 13 GB free, in a paragraph otherwise written in the present.
